assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks unite quantum control with an exceptionally consequential advance in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the decisive magic-wavelength clock architecture, while Ye made foundational experimental advances and broad realization possible.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature, reproducible internationally, and has set the frontier for optical timekeeping.
uncertainties: The proper division of credit among the wider optical-clock community requires careful historical review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made the interaction of individual artificial atoms and microwave photons controllable on a chip, opening a genuinely new experimental quantum-optics regime.
assessment.attribution: Blais provided the central theoretical formulation; Wallraff and Schoelkopf led landmark experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: Its basic physics has been repeatedly confirmed and is now a durable platform for quantum optics and information.
uncertainties: The field has many indispensable contributors, so the limited laureate allocation is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the conceptual route by which fragile quantum systems can in principle support reliable computation.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Steane, and Kitaev each made distinct foundational contributions to codes and fault-tolerant architectures.
assessment.maturity: The theory is firmly established and experimental demonstrations are increasingly persuasive, although large-scale fault tolerance remains ahead.
uncertainties: Whether present experimental progress is sufficient to regard fault-tolerant computation as fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum computing transformed a clean atomic system into a highly controllable processor and a laboratory for quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller established central theoretical proposals, while Blatt delivered sustained leading experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: The platform has achieved high-fidelity control and independent replication over decades.
uncertainties: Credit must distinguish foundational trapped-ion computing from the broader quantum-information enterprise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-lattice quantum simulation has made strongly interacting many-body Hamiltonians experimentally programmable and observable.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Dalibard, and Greiner represent major and complementary experimental leadership in establishing the field.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, widely reproduced, and has yielded clean observations inaccessible in ordinary solids.
uncertainties: The foundational theoretical and experimental credit is unusually broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade turned strong neutral-atom interactions into a powerful controllable many-body and computing platform.
assessment.attribution: Saffman and Lukin made key conceptual contributions, and Browaeys has been central to definitive programmable-array experiments.
assessment.maturity: Large arrays and coherent control are now compelling and replicated, though the computing promise is still developing.
uncertainties: It remains uncertain whether the eventual fundamental legacy will be quantum simulation, computing, or both.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent optical detection and control of individual nitrogen-vacancy spins created an unusually practical bridge between quantum coherence and nanoscale sensing.
assessment.attribution: Jelezko and Wrachtrup were central to establishing single-defect optical spin control and its physical consequences.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena are robust, extensively reproduced, and broadly used in quantum sensing.
uncertainties: The extent to which the advance should be rewarded as fundamental physics rather than an enabling measurement technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics and quantum acoustics brought engineered mechanical motion into the quantum regime and enabled striking tests of measurement and control.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg, and Cleland made major complementary contributions spanning cavity optomechanics and quantum mechanical devices.
assessment.maturity: Quantum control of mechanical systems is experimentally secure across several architectures.
uncertainties: The discovery boundary between optomechanics, quantum acoustics, and related electromechanical work is broad.
